A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OATS by the same authors. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model and vision-transformer pruning experiments, ablations, CPU throughput measurements and attention visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds model evaluations, mechanism ablations, compression-time measurements and alternative-protocol perplexity results.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains second-moment scaling, alternating truncated SVD and hard thresholding, inverse scaling, and the same rank/sparsity allocation. Row-wise and N:M options already appear in v1. v2 clarifies their description and tests alternative procedures as ablations without replacing OATS.

E1.justification: Both use C4 calibration, the same ten-subject MMLU subset, eight zero-shot tasks, WikiText-2, ImageNet and COCO visualizations. Llama-3 70B and Qwen additions evaluate further model configurations on retained tasks; they do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: SparseGPT, Wanda and DSNoT remain the evaluated comparators, including the two DSNoT initializations in corresponding appendix comparisons. Added model evaluations use the same comparator set. Newly discussed methods such as SLOPE and SLIM are related work, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds Llama-3 70B and Qwen 2.5 3B Instruct configurations, Phi-3 Medium at 60% compression, a 20-iteration 70B experiment and broader rank/compression settings. Appendix A.12 additionally evaluates WikiText-2 with different normalization and segmentation. This supplements the retained LM Harness evaluation rather than replacing its protocol.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's scaling, row-wise pruning and hyperparameter studies, v2 adds tests of median-based scaling, reversed thresholding order and scaling only the low-rank component (A.3–A.5). Additional rank-ratio configurations and the reduced-iteration 70B experiment examine sensitivity and the compression-cost tradeoff.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. Added experiments retain point-estimate reporting; task averages and the median-scaling ablation do not constitute uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores are retained, while v2 adds substantial model, timing and ablation results. For example, new 50%-compressed Llama-3 70B MMLU accuracy is 74.79 versus DSNoT's 72.76 (Table 2); median scaling yields 55.54 versus standard scaling's 59.99 on Phi-3 Mini (Table 11). Table 18 adds perplexities under another protocol, so its lower values are not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds an asymptotic time-complexity expression and defines its dependence on matrix dimensions and rank. Algorithm 2 repairs the dimensionally inconsistent activation multiplication, and N:M wording changes from N zero entries to N nonzero entries. The core optimization remains unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The main claims about retraining-free compression, performance through 60% compression, CPU acceleration and complementary attention patterns remain. The conclusion adds an explicit priority claim that this is the first work to reveal the potential of sparse-plus-low-rank decompositions for large-scale transformers, broadening v1's method-specific novelty claim.

C2.justification: v2 acknowledges greater offline compression time and argues that deployment benefits justify this cost (A.2). It also explains why preserving outliers may matter more than minimizing activation reconstruction error (A.1), interprets the robust-scaling test, and discusses greater pruning resilience in vision transformers. Existing attention-rollout interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly supplies an OATS code-repository link, NVIDIA A40 hardware and memory specifications, compression timings and parallelization details. It documents Qwen hyperparameters and identifies the implementation used for alternative perplexity evaluation. Existing calibration, baseline settings and attention-rollout details are retained after relocation.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.1 substantially expands positioning against earlier CNN sparse/low-rank compression, vision-transformer pruning, SLOPE pretraining and concurrent SLIM compression. It distinguishes objectives, training requirements and decomposition procedures. v2 also adds GoDec attribution and further outlier-related citations while retaining the earlier related-work discussion.

P1.justification: v2 extensively revises contributions, method explanations, experimental narration, related-work prose and the conclusion. It creates a dedicated alternative-sparsity subsection, separates structured-pruning discussion and reorganizes the appendix, relocating existing task and implementation sections. These editorial changes extend beyond inserting new experimental content.

P2.justification: v2 expands model columns and appendix tables and adds displays for timings, ablations, hyperparameters, Qwen and alternative perplexity evaluation. Table 15 redisplays benchmark differences. Figures 1–2 revise axes and layout while retaining their plotted results; attention images remain unchanged. Original appendix Tables 9–11 map to Tables 17, 19 and 20.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence and practical documentation. New mechanism ablations address the basis of outlier scaling, larger-model and Qwen evaluations broaden validation, and A.2 supplies compression-cost information absent from v1. The code link, expanded prior-work comparisons and explicitly distinguished perplexity protocols further improve reproducibility and interpretation. A material weakness remains: the retained blanket MMLU superiority statement conflicts with the new 30% Llama-3 70B result, where Wanda outperforms OATS. This inconsistency does not outweigh the substantial evidential and documentation gains.
